title: Which angle is greater, Case one or Case two?
description: A book cover is opened a little in Case one and wider in Case two, and the two angles are compared by the amount of turn. The pages stay as the first ray and the cover is the second ray that turns about the hinge. Keeko's doubt, that both angles are the same because it is the same cover, is broken by the two openings that differ while the cover length stays equal.
teaching_notes: One idea: the size of an angle is the amount of turn about the vertex, not the length of its arms. Watch for students who say two angles are equal because the same cover makes both.

source: Which angle is greater: the angle in Case 1 or the angle in Case 2? Just as we talk about the size of a line based on its length, we also talk about the size of an angle based on its amount of rotation. So, the angle in Case 2 is greater as in this case she needs to rotate the cover more.
video_script.why: The child compares two angles by the amount of turn of the cover about the hinge.
video_script.substitution: Keep the pages as the first ray and turn the cover as the second ray.
video_script.anchor: the book of Ruhee, with the cover opened a little in Case one and wider in Case two
video_script.wrong_answer: both angles are the same because it is the same cover
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says both angles are the same because it is the same cover. The two cover rays are shown with equal length marks but different openings, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The angle in Case two is greater, because the cover is turned more

final_answer.value: The angle in Case 2 is greater, because the cover is rotated more
final_answer.spoken: the angle in Case two is greater, because the cover is turned more

names.Ruhee: the book's character who opens the cover of the book in six cases

never_show: which of the two angles is greater, before the answer beat
maths_rules: The size of an angle is the amount of rotation, or turn, needed about the vertex to move the first ray to the second ray.
The pages are the first ray and the cover is the second ray, and both start at the hinge.
In Case one the cover is turned a little, and in Case two it is turned more.
More turn means a greater angle, so the angle in Case two is greater.
Slip: the length of the cover is the same in both cases, but length does not decide the size of an angle.
video_script.design: One idea: more turn about the vertex means a greater angle. The book stays on the board and the cover is shown in Case one and Case two. The wrong idea is that the angles are equal because the cover is the same.
